note: This is the open-design successor to the saturated bdt-tranche-expander contract. Four counted arms ran sequentially in isolated single sessions with the same task and CDM 7.0.0 seed. Claude Code 2.1.227 used claude-sonnet-5 and local Claude Max authentication; Codex CLI 0.147.0 used gpt-5.4 and local ChatGPT authentication. All ran at high effort with API credential/provider overrides removed. Controls could not read cdm-dev, the repository, historical benchmarks, global skills, or sibling workspaces. Every authored suite passed from a clean offline copy before adaptive tests were introduced. Claude Fable 5 then independently inspected code and traces, reran the suites, and reviewed generated CDM validation. It scored Sonnet treatment/control 92/84 and GPT-5.4 treatment/control 89/70. All four missed the frozen non-later-tap guard. GPT control additionally rejected a genuine valid LEI, populated unsupported seniority/principal facts, and duplicated the CDM dependency. GPT treatment used a richer version-correct TransferableProduct boundary and passed six targeted generated data rules. The skill therefore delivered a modest Sonnet quality gain at a large time cost and a material GPT-5.4 correctness/modelling gain at a smaller time cost.
